We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{\infty }\frac{18}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{3}^{a}\frac{18}{{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =18{lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{3}^{a}{x}^{-4}\,\text{d}x \\  & =18{lim}_{a\to \infty }{[(-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3})]}_{3}^{a} \\  & =-6\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}]}_{3}^{a} \\  & =-6\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{{a}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{3}^{3}}) \\  & =-6(0-\frac{1}{27}) \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
